unit.why: An exemplary tale, copied from Shem Yaakov, about a pre-Hasidic pious man near Venice. He appears after death in a dream and reveals that he was punished in the heavenly court for mispronouncing his prayers, so the town hires a grammarian.
unit.boundary_note: trailing 'מענין דרך' is a section heading belonging to the next division

stories.start_quote: איש אחד היה מחסידי עליון ואספר
stories.end_quote: ולכל ישראל עד ביאת הגואל אמן
stories.summary_en: R. Ezra ben Yedidyah, a saintly ascetic near Venice, appears in dreams after his death to his friend R. Gedalyah. He tells him that his lapses in kavvanah were forgiven through his fasts, but that the mispronounced vowels and letters of his prayers accused him and he was sentenced to wander. The townspeople then hire the grammarian R. Moshe Hayyim to teach them correct pronunciation, and their prayers are accepted.
